notes:
THE WALKTHROUGH IS ONE PARAGRAPH, NOT BULLETS. There is nothing to number, so source_bullets [1] on every step means 'the single Walkthrough paragraph'. Flagged walkthrough_in_prose so a reader is not left thinking the citations are wrong.

THE ??? IS EXAMINED TWICE AND THAT IS ONE RUNG. You click it to plant a bomb, the bomb 'will explode after quite a while', and then you must check the SAME ??? again for the experience points and the message 'The stronghold has sustained considerable damage.' -- 'Failure to do so will result in the Ops Mission being a failure.' Two clicks on one unmarkable, unobservable object separated by a wait is one step with the cycle in the note, not two rungs the runtime could never tell apart. No `wait` rung either, for the same reason: nothing to mark and nothing to observe.

ZONE AND GRID COME FROM THE 'List of ???s' SECTION, whose bullets restart at [1]: 'Beaucedine Glacier (S): (I-8) (ENE Side)'. The paragraph itself only says 'a Beastmen controlled area in the Northlands, such as Beaucedine Glacier (S)' -- 'such as' means other Northlands strongholds presumably work too, and the page names exactly one, so that is the one recorded and the generality is flagged or_branch_unmodelled. Flagged grid_from_after_section because the only thing that section supplies is the location -- no step comes from it.

CAMPAIGN RANK is a real gate with no schema field: this page's field is {{question}} -- the wiki saying the rank requirement is unknown, not that there is none. It is NOT gates.level (which means character level, and this page's Level field is '70+'), so it lives here and in review_flags.

LEVEL: '70+' is a character-level gate with no job attached, so gates.level = 70 and gates.jobs stays []. Unit Requirement '1' has no schema field. The two Notes bullets are failure modes (the ??? works with no fortification present; the ??? can reset mid-bomb and start saying 'You find nothing out of the ordinary', which fails the op) -- warnings, not steps. Medium because the rank gate is unknown and unmodellable and the target zone is an example rather than a fact.

notes:
THE WALKTHROUGH IS ONE PARAGRAPH, so source_bullets [1] everywhere means that paragraph. Flagged walkthrough_in_prose.

THE FROST BOMB IS A `spawn`, NEVER A `kill`. Examining the ??? makes a Frost Bomb appear 'and attacks immediately', and the page is explicit: 'Do not attack the Bomb, but do not let it despawn/deaggro/stay unclaimed either.' You walk it to the fortification and it detonates itself with Hypothermal Combustion. Recording it with role 'kill' would tell core/kills.lua to want a corpse and would draw a sword glyph over the one mob in this op you must not fight, so role is 'spawn' and count 1, on the step that spawns it.

OR BRANCH: two locations, Beaucedine Glacier (S) at (H-9) 'down the ramp near the Campaign Arbiter and to the left when going down the ramp', or Xarcabard (S) at (G-10). One zone per step and no OR in the schema, so the Beaucedine entry is modelled (it is the one the page describes in detail) and Xarcabard is in the note.

THE DESTINATION HAS NO NAME I CAN USE. The page says 'Run to the Campaign Fort with the Frost Bomb'. 'Campaign Fort' is a description of the fortification you are attacking, not an entity name the page establishes, and any string in target.name becomes a live marker key, so that step is {"type": "none", "name": null} with the instruction in the note. Flagged generic_npc_name.

THIS PAGE HAS NO WALKTHROUGH SECTION AT ALL -- the cached wikitext is the {{Campaign Header}} template and nothing else. The ladder is read from the header's Orders field, which on this page is unusually complete and states the objective and the hand-in in words: 'Join a Campaign Battle in a Windurst-controlled area.' / 'Earn a total of 2000 Allied Notes with Allied Tags.' / 'When enough points have been earned, the message "Objective completed. Report to Emhi Tchaoryo in Windurst Waters." will appear when Allied Tags wear off.' source_bullets [1], [2], [3] therefore number THOSE three lines, not walkthrough bullets -- there are none. Flagged both walkthrough_incomplete and steps_from_header_orders. Medium and not low: the page really does say what to do; it just says it in the infobox.

THE MIDDLE STEP HAS NO TARGET AND NO ZONE, and both nulls are assertions. 'A Windurst-controlled area' is whichever Campaign zone the Confederate is besieging today -- not a zone name, and control changes week to week -- and there is no entity to interact with, so {"type": "none", "name": null}. Nothing draws a marker, which is the honest outcome; an invented zone or an invented NPC would draw a wrong one.

2000 ALLIED NOTES IS NOT OBSERVABLE. Allied Notes are a currency total, not an item you hold, and no packet reports the running score, so evidence is null and the count lives in the note. Flagged count_unobservable.

notes:
SIX ORCS, IN TWO GROUPS OF THREE, AND THE COUNTS ARE PER-OP NOT PER-GROUP. Bullet 4 says 'Two groups of three Orcs (six total)' and then describes ONE group in its sub-bullets: an Orcish Carrier plus 'Orcish Grunt x2'. Across both groups that is Orcish Carrier x2 and Orcish Grunt x4, which is the six the page counts and the six bullet 5 wants defeated. Notes bullet 2's 'All 3 of the Orc are Susceptible' is the same per-group arithmetic seen from the other side, not a third figure. This is where the sibling pages diverge and must not be copied: Pit Spider I (S) is a single line of THREE orcs, and the (B) line of the same op fights Quadavs.

'Vunkerl Inlet' IS NORMALISED TO 'Vunkerl Inlet (S)'. Bullet 2 drops the suffix; the bare form does not resolve (checked with tools/pipeline/resolve.lua: 'Vunkerl Inlet' -> no id, 'Vunkerl Inlet (S)' -> 83), and Wings of the Goddess campaign zones all carry it. The page's own Description links the same place as [[Vunkerl Inlet (S)]] on the sibling Pit Spider I (S), so the suffix is the page family's own spelling and not an import.

THE ENTRANCE OBJECT IS NAMED DIFFERENTLY HERE THAN ANYWHERE ELSE. This page calls it 'the Beastmen Stand at (J-7) in Vunkerl Inlet'; no other page in the cache uses that phrase. Pit Spider I (S) puts [[Beastman Ensign]] at the SAME (J-7) in the same zone, Pit Spider II (W) uses [[Beastman Ensign]] for the Fort Karugo-Narugo entrance, and the cached Category:Campaign Ops page explains the naming scheme outright: the instanced-area entrances are 'named [[Allied Ensign]], [[Beastman Ensign]], or [[Fortilace]], based on Op type'. Since any string in target.name becomes a live marker key with nothing to validate it against, I used the corroborated 'Beastman Ensign' and recorded this page's wording here and in the step note. Flagged entity_name_conflict.

THE EXIT KEEPS THIS PAGE'S SPELLING. 'Twilight Aureole' appears twice on this page (bullet 6 and Notes bullet 6) and on Pit Spider I (S), Pit Spider II (W) and By Light of Fire I (W); the (B) pages and Category:Campaign Ops spell the same object 'Twilight Aureola'. Neither spelling has a BG Wiki page of its own (both fetch 404 through the REST API), so there is no tiebreak, and unlike the Ensign there is no third name in play -- so each record keeps its own page's spelling and this note records the split.

TIME: the header says '30 minutes' and Notes bullet 1 says 'There seems to be no time limit'. Read carefully these are not quite the same claim -- the note is scoped to how long you may take GETTING to Everbloom Hollow, the header to the op -- but the page does not reconcile them, so it is recorded as an unresolved tension and the record is medium, not high.

CAMPAIGN RANK is a real gate with no schema field: 'Brass Ribbon of Service §§'. It is NOT gates.level (which means character level, and this page's Level field is 'Any'), so it lives here and in review_flags.

Bullet 3 ('once the party leader has selected to enter...') is the consequence of touching the Ensign, so it merges into step 2 rather than becoming a rung of its own. The failure list in Notes bullet 7 (leaving before the kills, warping out after them) is why the exit step is a real rung and not decoration.

two groups of three start running for their designated ends the moment you arrive: one Orcish Carrier and two Orcish Grunts each, so 2 and 4 across the op, six in total. The Carrier occasionally runs off mid-fight and the Grunts link with it; both are susceptible to Sleep and Gravity and have roughly 2500 HP. If a Carrier reaches the end of the area -- smaller here than in Pit Spider I (S) -- the op fails, and the Orcs warp out if you are too slow.

the page bolds this and repeats it in Notes bullet 6: leave through the Twilight Aureole or the op does not count. Warping out straight after the kills fails it. Spelled 'Aureole' here as this page spells it; the (B) siblings and Category:Campaign Ops write 'Twilight Aureola' for the same object.

Bullet 2 (he asks which craft you specialise in) and bullet 3 (he then tests you on three synths, with the six question forms listed as sub-bullets) are consecutive turns of one conversation with one NPC in one spot, so they are one step -- wedging a second rung between two talks to the same NPC buys nothing and splits a single marker.

Same zone as the giver, established rather than inherited.

REPEATABLE IS TRUE AND THE PAGE SAYS SO IN WORDS. {{Campaign Header}} has no Repeatable field, so this would normally be null -- but Notes bullet 1 states it outright: 'This is repeatable (as long as you have tags), making it a very quick and easy way to stock up on Allied Notes.' That is the page stating it, not me inferring it from the op being a Campaign Op. gates.expansion stays null; nothing on the page names an expansion.

Only three real rows exist (Buckler; Mythril Sallet; Tsurugitachi). It is a cheat sheet for the quiz, so nothing from it enters items or evidence -- you are asked to name ingredients, not to hold them.

notes:
THREE RUNGS: Hieronymus, one Campaign Arbiter, Hieronymus. Bullets 1, 2 and 3 are all the SAME NPC -- go to an Arbiter, give the crystal orders, then talk to that Arbiter again to be teleported home -- so they merge into one step rather than three rungs on one marker.

THE ARBITER STEP HAS NO ZONE AND THAT IS THE POINT. The page says 'go to any Bastok controlled area', which is not a zone name and changes with the war; Campaign Arbiters stand in every campaign zone. Zone is therefore null -- an assertion that the page gives none -- while the target keeps the real, page-stated NPC name so the marker can find whichever Arbiter you are standing near. Naming one zone would send players to a front the beastmen may hold this week.
